before: tryCatch evaluates an expression and uses a matching handler when a condition is signaled. error = function(e) receives the error object; its return value becomes the tryCatch result. The failed function does not resume at its next statement.

Here -1 is a deliberate sentinel outside the allowed positive domain. Real code can instead return a structured result with status and message. Catch errors only where you can handle them; blanket fallback values can hide defects.
Expected output or behavior: -1. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Use conditionMessage(e) in a handler to preserve a diagnostic alongside a status. You may trace it without a R interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
